# Label

The visible name of a form control.

<p class="odv-compstatus"><span class="odv-pill">In Content first</span></p>

## When to use it

**In Content first:** Names every field.

- **Use it when:** Every form control.
- **Not when:** Never skipped: a placeholder is not a label.

Instead:

- [Field](./field.md): The label laid out with hint and error.

## How Content first uses it

<div class="odv-grid two"><div class="odv-dd"><div class="stage"><div class="odv-eyebrow">Field label or column header</div><div style="margin-top:6px"><b style="color:var(--color-status-success)">Use</b> type.label</div><div><b style="color:var(--color-status-danger)">Not</b> type.caption</div></div><div class="cap">Caption is too faint for a label people must read.</div></div></div>

## Words

- Write to one person: "you", not "users".
- Short sentences with room to breathe.
- Explain why before asking for anything.
- Use: Read, Save for later, You, Next issue. Avoid: Click here, Submit, Users, Content.

The labels components use, from the voice tokens:

- `content.action.commit`: Save
- `content.action.cancel`: Not now
- `content.action.destroy`: Remove
- `content.action.retry`: Try again
- `content.action.empty-action`: Browse guides

See [Voice and tone](../voice.md) for the whole voice.

## Accessibility and keyboard

Test before you ship:

- [ ] The label is linked to its control and makes the hit area larger. undefined

## Use it in code

```bash
npx open-ds add label
```

The component reads only component keys and semantic tokens, so it follows the brand and mode on `<html>`.

## Variables

Every token Label reads, from its code: the variable, the semantic token it aliases, and where that ends in the theme.

### Read straight from the system

Label has no variables of its own yet; it reads these system tokens directly.
